As of 330 AM EST Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Significant impacts will continue through the 
morning and early afternoon before winds begin to decrease and the 
heaviest rainfall lifts north of the region.

The forecast is largely on track this morning with impacts ongoing 
across the region. All wind and flooding headlines are unchanged 
with this forecast package. Early morning analysis shows an 
impressive pressure gradient across the area between 1044mb high 
pressure anchored over the Northeast and 1000mb low pressure near 
Wilmington, NC. Check of surface observations along the NC coast 
reveal 10-12mb pressure falls over the last 6 hours. 00z guidance 
has backed off a tad with respect to how deep the surface low will 
get, with most models showing the low ~997mb at peak intensity this 
morning into the afternoon. 

Moderate to heavy rainfall covers the entire area with the heaviest 
precip expected to lift northward through the morning hours. Storm 
total precip remains similar to previous forecasts, in the 2-5" 
range with localized 6" totals possible. The Flood Watch will 
continue through early this afternoon for the majority of the area 
and into late afternoon for NE portions. WPC has expanded the Slight 
Risk (level 2/4) ERO north and west into the Richmond Metro, Tri-
Cities, and I-64 corridor back into Fluvanna and Louisa Counties. 
Flash flooding is most likely in urban and poor drainage areas, 
especially with as any remaining leaves come down in the coincident 
strong winds and clogging drainage systems. The low moves 
into/across the region this afternoon with decreasing winds and 
precip.

Winds will continue to increase as we head toward sunrise and low 
pressure lifts NW into central NC. High Wind Warnings continue near 
the bay/coast with Wind Advisories for the remainder of the area. 
Northeast winds are forecast to gust to 40-50 mph inland and 55-65 
mph near the coast. While 925mb wind fields are even higher than 
this ~70 kt/80 mph, not all of this be able to mix to the ground. 
Nevertheless, expect scattered to widespread power outages/tree 
damage near the coast, with at least some degree of impacts inland 
with the higher end advisory level winds. Impacts in the Wind 
Advisory area inland will be greater than what occurs during our 
typical Wind Advisories. We are already starting to see some power 
outages across the region, even well away from the coast in areas 
near the I-95 corridor. The strong E-NE winds continue for much of 
the morning before diminishing and becoming SE during the afternoon.

While the very strong synoptic wind and heavy rain are the most 
widespread concerns, we are still monitoring the threat for severe 
weather. With a farther west low track, a larger portion of the area 
gets into the warm sector of the system later this morning into the 
afternoon. After the main area of rain exits from south to north, 
there remains uncertainity whether additional convection can develop 
in the warm sector during the midday/afternoon. Some of the models 
show this, while others do not. With temps rising into the lower 70s 
and dew pts in the mid-upper 60s in the warm sector, instability is 
expected to increase to a few hundred J/kg of MLCAPE at least in SE 
VA/NE NC. With the strong kinematic fields in place and low-level 
winds becoming SE, any storm that manages to develop in the warm 
sector will pose at least a low-end threat for a brief tornado. SPC 
has maintained a Marginal (Level 1/5) Risk for severe weather in 
areas near the bay/coast in addition to NE NC. 
 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Significant coastal flooding is expected today into 
Friday, with widespread moderate to major flooding and potentially 
record water levels at a few locations.

Significant coastal flooding is expected today into Friday, with 
widespread moderate to major flooding and potentially record water 
levels at a few locations. 

A significant coastal flooding event is unfolding across the region 
early this morning as strong E-NE winds associated with deepening 
low pressure near the NC coast combine with elevated astronomical 
tides. Coastal Flood Warnings remain in effect across the tidal 
forecast area, with widespread moderate to major flooding expected. 

The latest forecast still supports potential historic flooding as 
several locations, especially along the Atlantic-facing Eastern 
Shore and portions of the tidal James River. Forecast water levels 
at Wachapreague, Jamestown, and Lynnhaven could exceed their 
respective historical maxima. The most significant flooding is 
expected this morning into early afternoon at most locations. 
Additional high tide cycles will also be impacted into Friday, 
especially across the eastern shoreline of the Chesapeake Bay.
